title: Graceful Compute Fallbacks and SLA Declension Proposal
body:
Context and problem:

This is a working PRD sketch for a combined approach to: autoscaling, burst options, and isolation controls for Dedicated capacity. The goal is to make capacity behavior predictable for customers with long tail usage patterns (microbursts + sustained ramping), while protecting other tenants and preserving SLA guarantees.

Why this is different from existing drafts:
- Focus is on graceful, compute-first fallbacks (aka "declension" of SLA guarantees in a controlled way) rather than hard preemption or blunt throttles.
- Introduces the idea of sustained-throughput hedging credits (not just microburst credits) and model-fractionation as a means to preserve latency-sensitive requests when capacity thins.
- Emphasizes per-tenant isolation scoring and a small admission-controller shim to make on-the-fly routing decisions.

High-level goals:
- Keep 99th percentile latency SLOs for high-priority lanes under transient load spikes.
- Ensure fair long-term throughput between tenants (no tenant hogging during sustained surges).
- Provide predictable, explainable customer experience when Dedicated pools degrade: clear fallback lanes, metrics, and billing signals.
- Minimal operational overhead and simple console UX for admins to set policies.

Non-goals:
- This doc doesn't define low-level kernel/runtime optimizations (handled by serving-runtime team).
- Not covering private/VPC networking specifics.

Customer scenarios to cover:
1) A SaaS customer with periodic heavy sync jobs (10–20 min) that spike throughput for tens of minutes.
2) A bursty real-time chat provider with tight tail latency requirements for a subset of routes.
3) A tenant that runs large model evals unexpectedly and risks evicting production inference.

Principles and safety model:
- Graceful declension: when capacity drops, prefer strategies that reduce per-request compute (quantized variants, smaller model slices) or degrade non-tail-critical requests before terminating higher-priority requests.
- Credit separation: microburst credits (short-term) vs sustained hedging credits (minutes-hours). These should be tracked independently and decay at predictable rates.
- Isolation score: an online metric combining burstiness, historical unscheduled preemption impact, and priority tier. Used to bias admission and eviction decisions.

Key concepts:
- Hedging Credits: time-windowed tokens that allow a tenant to sustain above-commit for longer bursts. Purchased/allocated with reserved capacity or earned via historical good-behavior.
- Microburst Credits: short-lived tokens (seconds) for absorbing small spikes with no policy change.
- Model Fractionation: ability to route requests to a lower-compute variant of the same model (lower precision quant, smaller transformer width, sequence truncation) as a fallback lane.
- SLA Declension Lanes: cascading lanes with ordered fallback options: primary model on dedicated pool -> fractionated variant on dedicated -> hosted-compatible variant on shared pool -> queued or rate-limited.
- Isolation Score: numeric [0..100] per-tenant updated every minute. Higher score means more likely to be constrained.

Behavioral flow (runtime + control plane):
1) Admission controller receives request and tenant metadata (priority, model, route).
2) Look up active credits and isolation score. If under budget, allow into queue/batch; else consult hedging/microburst credits.
3) If no credits and dedicated pool is saturated, decide fallback according to tenant's rollback policy (configured in console). Options: auto-fractionate -> spill to hosted -> queue.
4) Emit clear audit event and user-facing metric: fallback_reason + fallback_depth. Also surface friendly console message and billing note.

Policy knobs for customers (console + API):
- reserve_commit: baseline GPU/slot reservation (current).
- sustained_hedge_minutes: how many minutes of over-commit allowed before enforced fractionation/queue (default 2 min).
- microburst_bank: number of short bursts allowed per hour (e.g., 120 bursts of 5s).
- fallback_order: ordered list e.g. [fractionate, spill_to_hosted, queue].
- isolation_bucket: static tier override to influence isolation score (manual admin control).

Operational signals and metrics to expose:
- per-tenant: isolation_score, hedging_credit_balance, microburst_balance, fallback_events{count,type}, avg_fallback_depth, eviction_count
- pool-level: sustained_overcommit_seconds, fractionation_rate, spill_ratio (requests spilled to hosted), queue_wait_seconds
- SLAs: 99p latency per-lane pre/post fallback, fractionated variant quality deltas (BLEU/ROUGE or custom eval metrics).

Console UX sketches (notes):
- Dedicated pool page shows a "health" ribbon with hedging consumption and projected hours-to-exhaustion.
- Tenant policy page includes an "impact preview" slider: set sustained_hedge_minutes and show simulated fallback events on historical traffic.
- Alerts: cost/hedging threshold (email/Slack) and automated rollback recommendation.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (labs): implement isolation_score and credit accounting in control plane. Add metrics only (no automatic fallbacks). Run for 6 weeks and validate signals against SLOs.
- Phase 1 (soft rollout): enable fractionation fallback for non-production routes and a small set of opt-in customers.
- Phase 2 (opt-in proactive): allow customers to enable hedging credits + fallback policies via console.
- Phase 3 (default): enable auto-fallback with safe defaults and clear billing rules.

Billing model implications:
- Hedging credits can be both purchased (prepaid add-on) or earned (loyalty credit). Purchased credits reduce risk for Redwood but require UI for purchase and tracking.
- Spill-to-hosted incurs cross-product billing: clearly show estimated cost delta before enabling.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regression: fractionation may degrade model outputs. Mitigate by requiring customers to opt-in to fractionation per-model and collect quality regression alerts (Redwood Optimize integration).
- Complex billing confusion: provide clear receipts, per-fallback cost line items, and an FAQ.
- Overcomplicated controls: default safe policies and a single "simple mode" toggle for small teams.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is the canonical decay function for hedging credits? Linear or exponential? (Action: SRE + product to prototype).
- How to compute isolation_score weights (burstiness vs historical impact)? (Action: data science experiment).
- UX: what wording reduces customer anxiety when we auto-fractionate? Draft copy needed.
- Compliance: do we need explicit customer consent to spill to hosted for regulated tenants? (Legal/Compliance to review).

Operational runbook snippets (starter):
- If a pool shows fractionation_rate > 10% for > 15m, create an incident with severity P2 and notify capacity-planning.
- If hedging_credit_balance across top-10 tenants is > 60% depleted, surface suggested scaling recommendation to sales/CS.

Notes to self / rough action items:
- Add simple simulation harness using past 30 days of traffic to model hedging exhaustion (Marco).
- Wire isolation_score to existing per-tenant telemetry (Ravi).
- Draft console mockups and copy (Diane).
- Legal check for spill-to-hosted (Jamal).

References and inspiration:
- internal: confluence:Dedicated-Capacity-Design (link above)
- slack: #dedicated-capacity-discuss thread (see JIRA-PI-4123 for context)
- related PRDs: tenant-traffic-containment-and-noisy-neighbor-mitigation-prd-wip.json (reviewed but this doc focuses on graceful fallback alternatives).

Status: Draft. Seeking feedback from serving-runtime (for model-fractionation feasibility), SRE (for credit decay patterns), and legal (hosting spill consent).
